clue.text: Lad rings doctor, first of all, in Indian port

indicators.note: to ring something is to encircle it, so one word goes round the others

parts.note: a lad is a boy
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

indicators.note: first of tells us to keep only the opening letter of the word that follows

parts.note: the opening letter of all

explanation.surface: A young man phones a doctor before anything else while in a port in India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rings' reads as telephoning, but here it means encircling: the lad's word goes round the doctor's qualification and the letter together.
explanation.definitionFit: Bombay, now Mumbai, is the great harbour city on India's west coast.

clue.text: George Nelson's record?

parts.note: surface reading: a disc or criminal file belonging to someone called George Nelson
setter's reading: the record of a gangster is his mugshot, and this gangster was famous for his youthful-looking features, which became his nickname

explanation.surface: Asks what a man named George Nelson recorded or has on file.
explanation.walkthrough: George Nelson was a 1930s American bank robber known by this nickname; 'record' hints at the police file and the face it shows.
explanation.definitionFit: The gangster's nickname came from his boyish, youthful-looking features, so the face on his police file is his nickname.

clue.text: US singer performed packing a lounge

indicators.note: something packing an item holds it inside, so one word sits within another

parts.note: to meet an obligation is to perform it, so performed can be met
taken as written
to lounge about is to loaf

explanation.surface: A singer from America gave a show while carrying a sofa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'performed' is used in the sense of carrying out or fulfilling, as when one meets an obligation.
explanation.definitionFit: Meat Loaf was the stage name of the American rock singer of Bat Out of Hell.

clue.text: Questions dance music around the South raised

indicators.note: in a down entry, raised means read from the bottom upward, so the letters run backward
around means going round something, so one word encloses the abbreviation

parts.note: ska is a Jamaican dance music
S is the abbreviation for South

explanation.surface: Someone queries dance music that is played around the southern part of a country.
explanation.definitionFit: To question someone and to ask them are the same verb, both in the third person here.

clue.text: At Danube, raging with no loss of intensity

indicators.note: raging suggests violent disorder, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A picture of the Danube in full flood, rushing on without weakening.
explanation.definitionFit: Unabated describes something that has not lessened, i.e. continuing at full strength.

clue.text: Civilians in wartime ban most cannot fancy

indicators.note: fancy as an adjective means elaborate or made up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Wartime restrictions forbid civilians most of the things they would like.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' reads as a verb meaning want, but it is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Noncombatants are people who take no part in the fighting, typically civilians during a war.

clue.text: Top actor almost becomes top author

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter of the name is dropped

parts.note: to top something is to best it
Peter Sellers was a British comic actor

explanation.surface: A leading performer nearly turns into a leading writer.
explanation.walkthrough: Peter Sellers, star of the Pink Panther films, loses his last letter: BEST + SELLER(S).
explanation.definitionFit: A bestseller is a writer whose books sell in very large numbers, so a top author in sales terms.

clue.text: Flap, in a manner of speaking

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the flap of leather under a shoe's laces

explanation.walkthrough: 'in a manner of speaking' looks like the idiom meaning 'so to speak', but it hides the second meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: A tongue is the flap on a shoe, and also a language, a particular way people speak.

clue.text: Alluring things, bashful cuddled by Des

indicators.note: something cuddled by another is held in its arms, so one word goes inside the name

parts.note: taken as written: a man's name
bashful means shy or coy

explanation.surface: A shy, attractive person is held close by a man called Des.
explanation.definitionFit: Decoys are lures that entice something into a trap, so they are things designed to allure.

clue.text: Australian bird — second seen round lake and river there

indicators.note: seen round means going around, so one word wraps the abbreviation

parts.note: to second a proposal is to back it
L is the abbreviation for lake
the Swan is the river of Perth, in Western Australia, 'there' pointing back to Australia

explanation.surface: A native bird of Australia is spotted at a second visit around a lake and its river.
explanation.definitionFit: The black swan is the native swan of Australia and the emblem of Western Australia.

clue.text: Referee, one trying to put a stop to foul play?

definitions.meaning: first meaning, literal: an official who blows a whistle

definitions.text: one trying to put a stop to foul play
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a person who exposes wrongdoing in an organisation

explanation.walkthrough: The second half reads like more about the match official, but 'foul play' also means crime or corruption that an insider exposes.
explanation.definitionFit: A whistleblower is an insider who reports wrongdoing; literally, a referee is the one blowing the whistle.

clue.text: Boy in charge of sound

parts.note: a boy is a son
i/c is the standard abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: A lad is put in control of the audio.
explanation.definitionFit: Sonic is the adjective meaning relating to sound or sound waves.

clue.text: Fellow with everything in sink

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fellow
everything means all

explanation.surface: A man throws everything into the kitchen sink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sink' looks like a basin, but it is the verb meaning go down.
explanation.definitionFit: To fall and to sink are both verbs for dropping to a lower level.

clue.text: Small-scale experiment undertaken by the aviation industry?

definitions.text: Small-scale experiment undertaken by the aviation industry?

parts.note: straight reading: a preliminary trial run before a full project
setter's reading: an investigation of aircraft flyers, as if the term were literal

explanation.surface: Imagines an airline doing a little trial research.
explanation.walkthrough: The trial-run term contains the word for someone who flies a plane, so the question mark invites reading it as aviation research.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilot study is a small preliminary experiment testing methods before a larger research project.

clue.text: Be unequalled racing on land and at sea, mostly

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter of the final word is dropped
racing suggests things whirling about, so the letters get mixed up

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
the word sea without its last letter

explanation.surface: A champion who has no rival in races both on land and on water.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand alone is an idiom for being unmatched, having no equal or rival.

clue.text: Device promoting fidelity in stately 'bitch', possibly

indicators.note: possibly hints at one of several arrangements, so the letters can be reordered

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Suggests a grand but spiteful lady might be kept faithful by such a contraption.
explanation.definitionFit: A chastity belt is a locked garment, legendarily used to keep a wife faithful during her husband's absence.

clue.text: Control lever girl's to click

parts.note: Joy is a girl's name, with the possessive S
a tick is a small clicking sound, as of a clock

explanation.surface: A lever that a girl uses to click things.
explanation.definitionFit: A joystick is the hand lever that controls an aircraft or a computer game.

clue.text: Put off drinking tin or bottle

indicators.note: something drinking takes another thing in, so one word swallows the other

parts.note: to put someone off is to deter them
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: Someone is discouraged from drinking out of a tin or a bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: A decanter is a glass bottle into which wine or spirits are poured for serving.

clue.text: So he returned abroad in secret

indicators.note: abroad can mean widely scattered, so the letters are spread into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man came back from overseas secretly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' looks like it could signal a reversal, but it is part of the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Under the rose (sub rosa) is an old idiom meaning confidentially, the rose being a symbol of secrecy.

clue.text: Deputy in the theatre

explanation.walkthrough: Both definitions are adjective-like: a deputy head is the acting head, and someone in the theatre may be acting.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting describes someone filling a post temporarily, and is also the profession of performing in plays.

clue.text: Greek with German man in cave

parts.note: Gr is the abbreviation for Greek
Otto is a typical German man's name

explanation.surface: A Greek and a German man shelter together in a cave.
explanation.definitionFit: A grotto is a small cave, often picturesque or artificial.

clue.text: Brief unwell, cutting down

parts.note: curt means brief or terse
ailing means sick

explanation.surface: A short illness forces someone to cut back.
explanation.definitionFit: Curtailing something means reducing or cutting it short, the same as cutting down.

clue.text: Land mass — between seas, I assume

indicators.note: between means lying among the following words, spanning the gap from one to the next

parts.note: the letters run across the end of seas, the I and the start of assume

explanation.surface: Someone guesses a continent sits between oceans.
explanation.definitionFit: Asia is the largest of the continents, the great land masses of the earth.

clue.text: Notice a blemish

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to see or detect
second meaning: a pimple or mark on the skin

explanation.walkthrough: Reads as an instruction to notice a flaw; in fact the verb and the noun are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: To spot is to catch sight of, and a spot is a small mark or pimple.

clue.text: Start in neutral in it on run out

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation inside the following word

parts.note: taken as written
N stands for neutral, as on a gear lever or electric plug
ro is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for run out

explanation.surface: A car's engine is started while in neutral, then it runs out of fuel.
explanation.walkthrough: Cricket scorers record a batsman dismissed by being run out as 'ro'. 'on' here means placed next to.
explanation.definitionFit: An intro is the opening section of a song or piece, its start.

clue.text: Direction given by particular Military Academy

parts.note: west is a compass direction
a particular is a detail or point

explanation.surface: Instructions handed out at a specific military college.
explanation.definitionFit: West Point, New York, is the site and common name of the United States Military Academy.

clue.text: George Martin's first, first from EMI to hear arrangement

indicators.note: first here means only the start of the name, so the tail of the word is cut off

parts.note: the start of the name George

indicators.note: first from tells us to take just the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: the opening letter of Martin
the opening letter of EMI
a court that hears a case tries it

explanation.surface: Sir George Martin, the Beatles' producer at EMI, listens first to a new musical arrangement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrangement' looks like a musical term or an anagram signal, but it is the definition. George Martin produced the Beatles' records for EMI.
explanation.definitionFit: The geometry of something is the arrangement or configuration of its parts, as in the geometry of a molecule.

clue.text: One fuelling the fire of Irish novelist?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a person who feeds coal into a furnace
second meaning: Bram, the Dublin-born author of Dracula

explanation.walkthrough: The 'of' makes it read like a fire belonging to the novelist; it just joins two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoker tends a furnace on a steam engine or ship, and Bram Stoker wrote Dracula.
